title: E: Report plant density, propagation and evolutionary change
description:
## What to build
Expose concise normal-run ecological statistics so slow evolution and resource balance are observable. Report per-species biomass and occupied-cell counts, successful establishments, mutation counts and biomass-weighted trait summaries relative to baselines. Separate per-tick events from cumulative totals and final population snapshots using existing Tick statistics semantics. Include growth versus transfers versus consumption accounting and document the initial parameter table. Avoid a new interactive view; use existing reporting surfaces and a seeded noninteractive diagnostic path where long runs are needed.

## Acceptance criteria
- Per-species biomass and occupied-cell totals agree with the final world snapshot, including mixed cells and extinct species.
- Growth, spread, grazing and mutation events are counted exactly once at their simulation resolution points; failed events do not inflate counts.
- Trait summaries reflect living local populations with sufficient precision to reveal tiny changes; zero-population output is defined.
- Per-tick values reset correctly and cumulative values persist; accounting reconciles biomass across ticks.
- Documented seeded diagnostic runs report plant and creature inheritance/mutation opportunities and realized changes over comparable ticks.
- Reporting regression tests and test/race/vet checks pass; normal terminal output remains readable.

title: F: Validate and tune the integrated textured plant ecosystem
description:
## What to build
Exercise the complete normal simulation and a noninteractive long-run scenario with all slices integrated. Validate resource invariants, deterministic runs, independent species textures under creature overlays, visible propagation fronts, mixed cells and slow local trait drift. Tune the parent baseline parameters only when recorded seeded evidence justifies changes; update the parameter table and explain tradeoffs. This is integration validation, not a substitute for tests in preceding slices. Use runs that can continue ecology observation beyond the normal creature-extinction/lineage stop condition without silently changing interactive stop behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fixed-seed scenarios show patch expansion, grazing clearings/regrowth, mixed-species boundaries and local heritable trait differences; multiple seeds characterize outcomes without promising permanent coexistence.
- Long runs preserve capacity, nonnegative biomass, bounded traits and accounting; repeat runs with the same seed reproduce world and statistics.
- Terminal review covers every species combination, all density bands and crowded creature/carnivore overlays, with exactly three columns per cell and no frame shimmer.
- Measured plant mutation frequency and magnitude are substantially lower per establishment than creature cloning; report realized per-tick behavior and adjust defaults if plants evolve too quickly.
- Compare tick/render performance against a recorded baseline on the default 38x81 world; investigate material regressions and record seed, run length and observations.
- go fmt ./..., go test ./..., go test -race ./... and go vet ./... pass; domain documentation and user-facing legend/defaults match shipped behavior.

title: D: Inherit rare bounded plant mutations during colony establishment
description:
## What to build
Add local heritable traits to successful colonization, using the parent evolution model. Founders use species baselines; successful daughter colonies copy the parent cohort and rarely mutate one trait. Do not mutate global species definitions or mutate established populations during ordinary growth. The altered growth/spread/nutritional traits must influence actual simulation outcomes, including grazing value and food-seeking decisions. Keep fixed species identity for visual recognition. Document the one-cohort-per-species-per-cell simplification and extinction/recolonization semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unmutated daughters inherit exact parent traits; an injected deterministic mutation changes at most one eligible trait by at most 0.25% and respects 80–120% bounds.
- Default mutation probability is 0.001 per successful establishment; failed attempts, regrowth and existing-colony rejection cannot mutate traits.
- Traits retain fractional precision, affect growth, spread or feeding as appropriate, and remain local to descendants rather than modifying unrelated colonies.
- Species identity and texture remain stable; fully extinguished local colonies lose their traits and later recolonization inherits the new parent.
- Controlled tests exercise inheritance, mutation boundaries and phenotype effects without flaky probability assertions; seeded sampling documents the rarity relative to creature clone mutations.
- Test/race/vet checks pass and the domain documentation explains plant generations and the intended slower evolutionary timescale.

title: A: Feed creatures from a shared-capacity three-species vegetation model
description:
## What to build
Introduce local grass/clover/bramble populations and shared growing capacity as the source of truth. Provide a runnable seeded world with all three species; integrate eating, food observation, movement ranking and tick statistics immediately. Until local propagation lands, retain local regrowth only for populations already present. Establish stable species ordering and read-only biomass/capacity/trait access for independent renderer and propagation work. Store fractional growth/nutrition progress without losing low-rate changes. Use baseline values in the parent epic. Herbivores consume at most five biomass units per action, highest current nutritional yield first with stable species-order ties; account for actual consumed biomass and cap nutrition. Food seeking compares total available nutritional value consistently, with documented conversions for existing thresholds. Carnivores never consume vegetation. Avoid a separately mutable scalar food cache.

## Acceptance criteria
- Running the simulation creates mixed-species populations and herbivores can consume each species using its baseline nutritional yield.
- All populations remain nonnegative and their combined biomass never exceeds shared capacity; zero-capacity and tiny-map cases are defined.
- Observation, movement selection, eating and reporting use the same plant source of truth; obsolete food/maxFood test fixtures are migrated.
- Eating mixed food produces exact biomass-consumed accounting and bounded nutrition, including partial/fractional cases; carnivore behavior remains correct.
- Species identity, local colony, biomass, capacity and nutritional value are documented; renderer/propagation consumers have a stable state contract.
- Deterministic integration tests pass along with go test ./..., go test -race ./... and go vet ./....

## Blocked by
None — can start immediately

title: B: Render consistent mixed-species textures beneath creatures
description:
## What to build
Render all three species in the normal map using the parent texture contract and the vegetation state delivered by A. Use stable three-column species positions to expose minority populations; reserve background identity/density under creature glyphs and draw texture only in unoccupied foreground positions. Use narrow, terminal-safe texture primitives with a documented ASCII fallback if needed. Provide a compact legend explaining species, density bands and the limitation that creature overlays hide foreground texture. No vegetation-view toggle. Keep rendering deterministic and independent from simulation RNG.

## Acceptance criteria
- Empty, sparse, medium and dense examples visibly progress from dark soil to richer species texture/background; each positive density band is documented.
- All single-species cases, three pairings, three-species mixtures and a trace population beside a dominant one remain distinguishable.
- Grass, clover and bramble use distinct patterns and colors rather than species-letter or plant-icon labels; no averaging species into ambiguous colors.
- Single and multiple creatures and carnivore brackets retain their existing identity cues over per-position plant backgrounds; every cell occupies exactly three terminal columns even for large creature counts.
- Unchanged vegetation renders identically across frames; rendering consumes no simulation randomness and resets ANSI state correctly.
- Representative terminal fixtures cover overlays and mixed densities, with recorded visual inspection plus width/ANSI regression checks; tests and vet pass.

title: C: Grow seeded plant patches through snapshot-based local propagation
description:
## What to build
Replace independent random food placement/regrowth with seeded patches, density-limited regrowth, species-specific local dispersal and shared-capacity competition using the parent starting parameters. Collect growth/spread intents from the tick-start plant snapshot, resolve them, then apply once before creature decisions. Prevent scan-direction cascades; define stable tie arbitration without permanent species priority and isolate random draws from traversal order. Existing same-species colonies reject colonization; other species may coexist. Establishment transfers parent biomass, so distinguish growth-created biomass from spread transfers in statistics. Seeded patch initialization must handle overlaps, boundaries and small maps explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria
- With a controlled seed, grass expands cardinally, clover into eight-neighbor gaps, and bramble within distance two; no new colony can spread again in its birth tick.
- An isolated empty region receives no plants without a reachable parent; a completely extinct species does not spontaneously reappear.
- Eligibility thresholds, attempt rates, target selection, establishment transfer and fractional density-limited regrowth match documented configuration.
- Simultaneous competing intents never exceed source biomass or destination capacity, do not always favor one species, and preserve multi-species cells where space exists.
- Seeded outcomes are repeatable; reversing candidate enumeration after stable event ordering produces equivalent plant updates.
- Growth, grazing and biomass-transfer accounting reconcile across ticks; long-run boundedness and edge/corner tests pass with test/race/vet checks.

title: Plant ecology: textured mixed vegetation and slow evolution
description:
## What to build
Deliver grass, clover and bramble with consistent density textures, mixed-species cells, creature-over-plant layering, local propagation and slow heritable evolution. All slices are AFK (implementable without a required human decision); manually inspect terminal output as part of visual verification. No vegetation-view toggle initially.

Starting design: three stable species positions in each existing three-column map cell. Species identity uses both texture and color: grass olive vertical texture; clover teal stipple; bramble muted-purple crosshatch. Texture primitives are terminal characters, not species-letter/icon labels. Dark soil at zero; positive density bands 1–9%, 10–39%, 40–69%, 70–100% of shared cell capacity, with increasing texture weight and background intensity. Each species retains its position even at low density. Creature foreground takes precedence; species backgrounds remain underneath.

Initial tuning values (explicit starting points, subject to seeded evidence): shared capacity 100 biomass units/cell; grass/clover/bramble intrinsic regrowth 0.08/0.04/0.02 biomass units per tick, nutrition 15/20/10 per consumed biomass unit, spread eligibility 20/30/40 local biomass, attempt probability 0.02/0.01/0.005 per eligible colony per tick. Grass targets cardinal neighbors, clover all eight adjacent neighbors, bramble offsets within Chebyshev distance two. One target per attempt, uniform among the species offsets; reject out-of-bounds, insufficient space, or existing same-species colonies. Successful establishment transfers one biomass unit from parent to target. No spontaneous reappearance after initialization. Grow existing populations with rate multiplied by free-capacity fraction, retaining fractional progress; allocate contested space without fixed species priority. Initial patches: per species max(1, ceil(cellCount/300)) centers, each with 20 biomass and adjacent halo cells with 5, within shared capacity; document small-map behavior.

Evolution: one local cohort per species per cell, inherited on successful colonization of a cell lacking that species. Existing same-species colonies are not overwritten or averaged by arriving propagules. Founders have base traits. A successful establishment has 0.1% mutation probability; at most one of regrowth rate, spread probability, or nutritional yield changes by up to ±0.25% relative, bounded to 80–120% of the species base. Preserve fractional traits so tiny changes are meaningful. Species identity, texture, spread neighborhood and threshold remain fixed initially. No mutation on tick entry, failed spread or ordinary regrowth. Compare documented per-establishment mutation rate and magnitude with current creature cloning (typically ±1% changes on each clone); quantify realized rates in seeded runs rather than promise a wall-clock timescale.

Dependency waves: A foundation -> B textures and C propagation in parallel -> D evolution after C (can overlap B) -> E ecology reporting after D (can overlap B) -> F integrated validation after B and E. Shared integration points may require merge coordination even where logical dependencies permit parallel work. Each slice updates domain documentation and includes its own meaningful tests; final validation covers cross-slice behavior. Use central RNG wrappers, snapshot/resolve plant updates, and keep mutation out of creature decision goroutines.

## Acceptance criteria
- All six child slices are delivered with recorded validation evidence.
- Normal map shows three plant species and their individual density cues, including mixed cells and creature overlays.
- Plants spread locally, compete for bounded capacity, feed creatures and transmit slowly evolving local traits.
- Domain terms, initial settings, evolution semantics, texture legend and dependency ordering are documented.

## Blocked by
None — can start immediately
